name: Psilocybin-Assisted Psychotherapy for Treatment-Resistant Depression
description: Psilocybin administered in a controlled therapeutic setting with preparation and integration sessions. Typically 1-2 dosing sessions with multiple non-drug therapy sessions. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation. COMPASS Pathways phase III trials ongoing.

name: Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy for End-of-Life Anxiety
description: Psilocybin therapy aimed at reducing existential distress, anxiety, and depression in patients with life-threatening illness. Landmark trials at Johns Hopkins, NYU, UCLA. Single high-dose session with preparation/integration.

name: MDMA-Assisted Psychotherapy for PTSD
description: MDMA administered in 2-3 sessions as an adjunct to psychotherapy for PTSD. FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation. MAPS (now Lykos Therapeutics) phase III trials showed 67% no longer met PTSD criteria after treatment. FDA decision pending/denied 2024.

name: Ketamine Infusion Therapy for Depression
description: Off-label IV/intranasal ketamine for treatment-resistant depression and acute suicidality. Spravato (esketamine) is FDA-approved. Widely available in US clinics (500+). Rapid onset (hours) but requires maintenance sessions.

name: Ibogaine Treatment for Opioid/Substance Use Disorder
description: Ibogaine, a psychoactive alkaloid from Tabernanthe iboga, used primarily for opioid detoxification/withdrawal and addiction interruption. Single prolonged session (24-36h). Significant cardiac risk (QT prolongation). Available in Mexico, Caribbean, and some non-US settings.

name: CRISPR-Based Gene Therapy (Somatic) for Genetic Disorders
description: Ex vivo or in vivo CRISPR gene editing for genetic disorders including sickle cell disease (Casgevy/Exa-cel approved), beta-thalassemia. Rapidly expanding pipeline. Casgevy FDA approved Dec 2023. First approved CRISPR therapy. Extremely high cost.

name: AAV9-Mediated Gene Replacement Therapy
description: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector-based gene replacement for monogenic disorders. Zolgensma (SMA, onasemnogene abeparvovec) is the landmark AAV9 therapy. One-time administration with potential lifelong effect. Several approved: Luxturna (retinal dystrophy), Hemgenix (hemophilia B), Elevidys (DMD), etc.

name: Mesenchymal Stem Cell (MSC) Therapy for Autoimmune/Inflammatory Conditions
description: MSCs derived from bone marrow, adipose, or umbilical cord tissue. Anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties. Used for osteoarthritis, Crohn's, MS, and numerous off-label indications. Regulatory status varies widely by jurisdiction. US: limited to approved trials and some orthopedic uses per FDA guidance.

name: CAR-T Cell Therapy for Hematologic Malignancies
description: Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell therapy: patient's own T-cells engineered to target cancer cells. Approved for B-ALL, DLBCL, multiple myeloma, and other blood cancers. One-time treatment with potential for durable remission. High cost, complex administration.

name: Medical Assistance in Dying (MAID) / Assisted Death
description: Medical assistance in dying encompasses physician-assisted suicide (patient self-administers) and voluntary euthanasia (clinician administers). Legal in Canada (MAID), Switzerland, Netherlands, Belgium, Spain, New Zealand, several US states, and others. Eligibility and safeguards vary significantly by jurisdiction. Canada's MAID expansion (2021-2027) has removed the requirement that death be reasonably foreseeable for some tracks.
typical_us_cost_range: Varies (covered by public health in some jurisdictions, $0-1,500 privately)

name: BPC-157 Pentadecapeptide Therapy
description: Body Protection Compound-157, a synthetic peptide derived from gastric juice protein. Promotes angiogenesis, accelerates wound/tendon/ligament healing, and shows protective effects in GI tract. Not FDA-approved. Widely used in functional/regenerative medicine but sold as 'research chemical' in US. Oral and injectable forms available. Evidence primarily preclinical with limited human trials.

name: Thymosin Alpha-1 (Thymalfasin) Immunomodulation
description: Synthetic 28-amino acid peptide identical to natural thymosin alpha-1. Modulates immune response, enhances T-cell function, and restores immune competence. Approved in 30+ countries (Zadaxin) for hepatitis B/C and as vaccine adjuvant. Used off-label for chronic infections, immune dysregulation, and cancer adjunct. Not FDA-approved in US.

name: In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) with Genetic Testing (PGT)
description: IVF with preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) or monogenic disorders (PGT-M). Enables embryo selection to avoid genetic disease transmission. Regulatory landscape varies: some countries restrict embryo genetic testing (Germany, Austria), others permissive (US, Mexico, Spain, Greece). Sex selection legally restricted in many jurisdictions.

name: Gestational Surrogacy
description: Gestational surrogacy where embryo is transferred to a surrogate who carries the pregnancy. Commercial surrogacy legal in parts of US (CA, NV, CT, etc.), Ukraine, Georgia, Colombia, Mexico (some states). Altruistic-only in Canada, UK, Australia. Completely banned in several EU countries. Complex legal landscape regarding parentage orders.

name: Low-Dose Naltrexone (LDN) for Chronic Inflammatory/Autoimmune Conditions
description: Naltrexone at low doses (0.5-4.5mg) acts as a glial cell modulator and transient opioid receptor blockade, leading to upregulation of endogenous endorphins and anti-inflammatory effects. Off-label use for fibromyalgia, Crohn's, MS, chronic pain, ME/CFS, long COVID. Requires compounding pharmacy. Decades of clinical use with strong safety profile at low doses.

name: Methylene Blue (Pharmaceutical Grade) for Neuroprotection/Mitochondrial Dysfunction
description: Methylene blue at low doses (0.5-4 mg/kg) acts as an alternative electron carrier in mitochondria, enhancing ATP production, reducing oxidative stress, and inhibiting tau aggregation. Being investigated for Alzheimer's (TauRx), bipolar disorder, and sepsis. Historical uses: malaria, methemoglobinemia. Pharmaceutical-grade required (NOT aquarium product).

name: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (Semaglutide / Tirzepatide) Beyond Diabetes
description: Originally for type 2 diabetes (Ozempic, Mounjaro), now FDA-approved for weight loss (Wegovy, Zepbound). Emerging evidence for addiction reduction (alcohol, opioids), cardiovascular risk reduction, neuroprotection (Alzheimer's), NAFLD/NASH, PCOS. Huge demand causing shortages. Compounded versions available but quality varies.

name: Rapamycin (Sirolimus) for Longevity/Healthspan
description: mTOR inhibitor with robust lifespan extension in every species tested. Approved as immunosuppressant (transplant) and for LAM (lymphangioleiomyomatosis). Off-label use for aging/longevity growing in popularity. PEARL trial (participatory evaluation of aging with rapamycin for longevity) ongoing. Intermittent dosing protocols emerging.
typical_us_cost_range: $50-200/month (generic, varies by dose protocol), $300-1,000/month (longevity clinic protocols)

name: Exosome Therapy (Stem Cell-Derived) for Regeneration
description: Exosomes (extracellular vesicles) derived from MSCs, containing growth factors, mRNA, and miRNAs that mediate paracrine signaling. Used for skin rejuvenation, hair restoration, joint repair, and systemic anti-aging. Less regulated than whole stem cells in many jurisdictions. Not FDA-approved. Rapidly growing aesthetics/regenerative market.

name: DMT (N,N-Dimethyltryptamine) Assisted Therapy for Depression
description: Short-acting (15-30 min) classical psychedelic. Proprietary extended-infusion formulation (SPL026/Small Pharma/incannex) in phase II trials for major depressive disorder. Naturally occurring in ayahuasca but synthetic DMT used clinically. Rapid onset/offset attractive for clinical delivery models. Colorado decriminalized personal use/growing 2022.
typical_us_cost_range: Unknown (clinical trials only, $3,000-8,000 estimated for infusion protocols)

name: LSD-Assisted Psychotherapy for Anxiety Disorders
description: LSD (lysergic acid diethylamide) administered in therapeutic setting. Historically used in psychiatry (1950s-60s) for anxiety, addiction, and existential distress. Modern renaissance: MindMed phase IIb for generalized anxiety disorder (MM-120). Switzerland permits compassionate use LSD therapy via BAG permits.
typical_us_cost_range: $5,000-12,000 (Switzerland compassionate use), unknown for US if approved

name: Mescaline-Assisted Therapy (San Pedro) for Depression/Addiction
description: Mescaline from San Pedro cacti in retreat settings. Natural plant medicine with centuries of ceremonial use. Longer duration (8-12h) than psilocybin. Emerging clinical interest. Colorado and other US states decriminalized mescaline-containing plants. Retreats in Peru, Colombia, Ecuador.

name: NAD+ IV Infusion for Mitochondrial Health/Longevity
description: Intravenous NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) infusions for mitochondrial energy, anti-aging, and neurological recovery. Off-label in US. High-dose protocols emerging (250mg-1000mg+). Biohacking/longevity community trending.

name: Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy for Chronic Wounds/TBI/Lyme
description: Breathing 95% oxygen in pressurized chamber (2-3 atm). FDA-approved for diabetic wounds, decompression sickness. Off-label expanding: chronic Lyme, TBI, fibromyalgia, post-COVID. Sessions 60-120 min, typically 20-40 sessions per course.
typical_us_cost_range: $150-350 per session, typical course $3,000-14,000. Insurance covers FDA indications.

name: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) for CDI/IBD
description: Fecal material from healthy donor transferred to patient's colon. FDA-approved for recurrent C. difficile. Off-label expanding: UC, Crohn's, IBS. >90% cure rate for CDI vs 30% antibiotics.
typical_us_cost_range: $500-3,000 per procedure. Covered by insurance for CDI indication.

name: PT-141 (Bremelanotide) for Sexual Dysfunction
description: Melanocortin-4 receptor agonist peptide. Vyleesi FDA-approved for female HSDD (2019). PT-141 original compound (research/compounded). Subcutaneous injection 45 min before sexual activity. Off-label for male ED growing.

name: Whole-Body Cryotherapy (WBC) for Recovery/Inflammation
description: Extreme cold (-110 to -200°C) exposure in cryogenic chamber for 2-3 minutes. Claims: inflammation reduction, recovery acceleration, mood boost. Growing biohacking adoption. Limited RCT evidence. Available in US and Europe.

name: Platelet-Rich Plasma (PRP) Therapy for Joint/Tissue Repair
description: Blood centrifugation to concentrate platelets (3-9x concentration) and inject into damaged joints/tissues. Growth factors (PDGF, VEGF, FGF) promote healing. Off-label use for osteoarthritis, tendon injuries, sports injuries. Some clinical trial data; evidence mixed but growing.
typical_us_cost_range: $500-2,000 per injection, typically 3-5 injections per course = $1,500-10,000

name: NMN/NR Oral Supplementation for Longevity
description: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) or nicotinamide riboside (NR) oral supplements to increase intracellular NAD+ levels. Promotes mitochondrial health, sirtuin activation. Emerging longevity trend. Limited RCT evidence in humans; strong preclinical data.
typical_us_cost_range: $30-100 per month (over-the-counter supplements), $500-2,000/year for clinical-grade protocols

name: Ayahuasca-Assisted Therapy for Depression/Addiction/Spiritual Growth
description: Ayahuasca (DMT + MAO inhibitor plants) consumed in ceremonial settings. 4-8 hour intense psychedelic experience with shaman facilitation. Growing clinical interest for depression, PTSD, addiction. Strong traditional use in Amazon. High variability in preparation and facilitation quality.

name: Medical Cannabis for Chronic Pain / Seizures / PTSD
description: Cannabis (THC/CBD) for medical indications. Legal status varies dramatically by jurisdiction. FDA-approved Epidiolex (CBD for seizures). Off-label use expanding: chronic pain, PTSD, anxiety, nausea. Dosing/strain selection critical. Quality dependent on legal vs. black market sources.

name: Ozone Therapy for Infection / Inflammation / Wound Healing
description: Medical-grade ozone (O₃) administered via autohemotherapy, insufflation, or bagging. Claims: anti-infection, anti-inflammatory, promotes healing. FDA does not approve ozone therapy (contraindicated in FDA statement). Off-label use growing in functional medicine. Highly variable quality/safety.

name: Neural Stem Cell Therapy for Neurodegeneration / Spinal Cord Injury
description: Neural stem cells (NSCs) derived from embryonic or iPSC sources for neurodegeneration (Parkinson's, ALS, Alzheimer's) and spinal cord injury. Preclinical data promising. Clinical trials ongoing in limited jurisdictions. Very high cost, experimental status.

name: Proton Beam Radiotherapy for Cancer
description: Proton beam therapy (vs. traditional photon radiation) allows precise tumor targeting with minimal normal tissue exposure. Lower side-effect profile. Approved for various cancers (pediatric, CNS, prostate, etc.). Limited availability—only ~50 centers in US, more in Europe/Asia. Extremely expensive.
typical_us_cost_range: $50,000-300,000+ (total course, varies by site and coverage)

name: Senolytic Therapy (Dasatinib + Quercetin) for Cellular Aging
description: Senolytic drugs eliminate senescent cells (aging-associated cells that promote inflammation). Dasatinib (tyrosine kinase inhibitor, FDA-approved for CML) + quercetin (polyphenol, OTC). Limited human trials but strong preclinical data. Mayo Clinic trial (UNITY) underway.
typical_us_cost_range: $50-150 per course (2 doses: quercetin OTC + dasatinib prescription)

name: IV Chelation Therapy for Heavy Metal Detoxification
description: EDTA or DMSA chelation to bind and eliminate heavy metals. FDA-approved for lead poisoning. Off-label promoted for autism, cardiovascular disease, aging ('detoxification'). Highly controversial—cardiologists warn against off-label use (risks: hypocalcemia, arrhythmias). Some functional medicine widespread adoption.

name: Metformin for Longevity / Aging Prevention
description: Metformin (FDA-approved type 2 diabetes drug) used off-label for aging prevention. TAME trial underway at NIH. Proposed mechanisms: AMPK activation, mTOR inhibition, improved metabolic health. Growing longevity community adoption.

name: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) for Depression
description: Noninvasive repetitive TMS (including deep TMS, iTBS) for treatment-resistant depression. FDA-cleared devices; widely covered when criteria met. Expanding off-label: OCD, smoking cessation, anxiety.

name: Deep TMS / TMS for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
description: TMS protocols cleared for OCD (e.g. deep TMS H7 coil). Adjunct when SSRIs/ERP incomplete.

name: Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS) for Depression
description: Implanted or transcutaneous VNS for chronic TRD. Implantable VNS has long FDA history for epilepsy and depression; noninvasive tVNS growing.

name: Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) for Parkinson's Disease
description: Stereotactic implantation of electrodes in STN/GPi for advanced Parkinson's motor complications. Established in high-income systems; access limited by neurosurgery capacity and cost.

name: MR-Guided Focused Ultrasound for Essential Tremor / PD Tremor
description: Incisionless thalamotomy using high-intensity focused ultrasound under MRI guidance. FDA-approved for essential tremor and PD tremor in selected patients.

name: Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocyte (TIL) Therapy for Melanoma
description: Autologous TILs expanded ex vivo then reinfused after lymphodepletion (e.g. lifileucel/Amtagvi). One-time cellular immunotherapy for advanced melanoma after checkpoint failure.

name: Experimental CAR-T / TCR Therapy for Solid Tumors
description: Investigational CAR-T/TCR products targeting solid tumors (e.g. Claudin18.2, GD2, mesothelin). Almost exclusively clinical trial or limited special-access pathways.

name: Dendritic Cell Cancer Vaccines (Personalized)
description: Autologous dendritic cells pulsed with tumor antigens. Sipuleucel-T is approved for prostate; many other DC vaccines marketed in less regulated clinics (quality highly variable).

name: Therapeutic Apheresis / HELP Apheresis for Long COVID & Microclot Protocols
description: Plasmapheresis, immunoadsorption, or heparin-induced extracorporeal LDL precipitation (HELP) used experimentally for post-acute COVID syndromes and microclot hypotheses. Evidence still evolving; not standard of care in most systems.

name: Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG) for Autoimmune / Neuroimmune Disease
description: Pooled IgG replacement/immunomodulation. Labeled for PID, ITP, CIDP, Kawasaki, etc.; widely used off-label (myositis, stiff-person, some long COVID clinics).

name: SGLT2 Inhibitors for Heart Failure & CKD Beyond Diabetes
description: Dapagliflozin, empagliflozin and related SGLT2i with strong HF and CKD outcome data independent of diabetes status. Access friction is mainly formulary/price, not legality.

name: GLP-1 Agonists for Alcohol / Substance Use Disorder (Emerging)
description: Semaglutide/tirzepatide prescribed off-label or studied for alcohol use disorder and other addictions. Evidence emerging; not a labeled SUD indication in most markets.

name: Prazosin for PTSD Nightmares
description: Alpha-1 antagonist used off-label for trauma-related nightmares. Inexpensive generic; evidence mixed across trials but widely used in veterans' care.

name: High-Dose Baclofen for Alcohol Use Disorder
description: Baclofen used off-label (sometimes high-dose protocols popularized in Europe) for alcohol dependence. France has had specific regulatory history; other countries physician discretion.

name: CJC-1295 / Ipamorelin Growth Hormone Secretagogue Peptides
description: Peptide secretagogues used in wellness/anti-aging clinics to raise GH/IGF-1. Not FDA-approved for these uses; compounding status restricted for many related peptides.

name: Tesamorelin (Egrifta) for HIV Lipodystrophy / Off-Label Visceral Fat
description: FDA-approved GHRH analog for reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-associated lipodystrophy. Off-label interest for visceral adiposity outside HIV.

name: Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy (MRT / Three-Person IVF)
description: Pronuclear or spindle transfer to prevent transmission of pathogenic mtDNA disease. Legal under regulated pathway in UK; largely prohibited or unregulated elsewhere.

name: Elective Oocyte Cryopreservation (Social Egg Freezing)
description: Planned oocyte freezing without medical indication (career/age planning). Legal in most developed markets; some jurisdictions restrict non-medical freezing or limit storage duration.

name: Uterus Transplantation for Absolute Uterine Factor Infertility
description: Living or deceased donor uterus transplant enabling pregnancy in AUFI (e.g. MRKH). Available only at specialized programs; high cost and ethical oversight.

name: 5-MeO-DMT Assisted Therapy
description: Short-acting intense psychedelic (synthetic or Bufo alvarius–derived). Clinical development emerging; ceremonial/retreat use in gray markets. High psychological intensity; toad-sourced product raises conservation/ethics issues.

name: Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy (KAP)
description: Structured psychotherapy wrapped around ketamine dosing sessions (distinct from infusion-only clinics). Practice standards vary; not a separate FDA approval from ketamine/esketamine.

name: Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) for Atrial Fibrillation
description: Nonthermal irreversible electroporation ablation for AF. Rapidly expanding after FDA clearances of PFA systems; availability lags in lower-resource systems.

name: Anti-Amyloid Monoclonal Antibodies (Lecanemab / Donanemab) for Early Alzheimer's
description: IV anti-amyloid mAbs for early AD with confirmed amyloid. Require APOE testing, MRI monitoring for ARIA. Coverage and capacity constrain access even where approved.

name: Testosterone Replacement Therapy (TRT) for Hypogonadism
description: Testosterone for clinical hypogonadism. Legal with prescription in most countries; telehealth and compounding gray markets common. Controlled substance in US (Schedule III).

name: Elamipretide / Mitochondrial-Targeted Peptides (SS-31 Class)
description: Mitochondria-targeted peptides (elamipretide and analogs) in development for Barth syndrome, mitochondrial myopathy, dry AMD, etc. Limited approved access; mostly trials/expanded access.
typical_us_cost_range: Trial or expanded access; commercial TBD

name: Elective / Bridge ECMO and Advanced Cardiac Support Tourism Pathways
description: ECMO is standard in major ICUs for severe cardiopulmonary failure. 'Tourism' angle is limited; arbitrage is capacity/expertise at high-volume centers rather than legality.

name: Elemental Diet / Rifaximin Protocols for SIBO (Access Friction Map)
description: Rifaximin (and combination protocols) plus elemental diets for small intestinal bacterial overgrowth. Drug access and insurance denials create practical arbitrage more than legality.
typical_us_cost_range: $1,000–2,500 for brand rifaximin course; elemental diet $500–1,000

name: Low-Dose Lithium for Neuroprotection / Mood
description: Sub-psychiatric doses of lithium (often lithium orotate OTC or low-dose carbonate) used for mood stability and putative dementia risk reduction. Full-dose lithium is prescription; microdose market is supplement/gray.

name: Psilocybin Microdosing Protocols
description: Sub-perceptual repeated dosing of psilocybin. Distinct from full-dose assisted therapy. Legal only where psilocybin is decriminalized/regulated; clinical evidence mixed.

name: Umbilical Cord Blood / Perinatal Cell Therapies
description: Banked cord blood for approved hematopoietic transplants; also marketed unproven perinatal cell infusions in regenerative clinics abroad.
typical_us_cost_range: Transplant standard of care (insured when indicated); clinic infusions $5,000–25,000

name: Near-Infrared Photoimmunotherapy for Head & Neck Cancer
description: Antibody-IR700 conjugate activated by near-infrared light (e.g. Japan-approved ASP-1929/Akalux pathway). Geographic access currently skewed to Japan and trial sites.

name: United States - Federal
general_notes: Federal law: Most psychedelics are Schedule I (no accepted medical use). Right-to-Try laws exist federally for terminally ill patients. FDA Expanded Access (compassionate use) program. ClinicalTrials.gov registration required for trials.

name: United States - Oregon
general_notes: Psilocybin Services Act (Measure 109, 2020). Regulated psilocybin therapy program operational since 2023. Also decriminalized personal possession of all drugs (Measure 110, 2020) though Measure 110 was partially rolled back in 2024.

name: United States - Colorado
general_notes: Proposition 122 (Natural Medicine Health Act, 2022). Regulated psilocybin therapy program, also decriminalized personal possession/growing of psilocybin, DMT, ibogaine, and mescaline (excluding peyote).

name: United States - California
general_notes: SB 519 (decriminalization of psychedelics) passed Senate, stalled. Multiple city-level decrim ordinances (Oakland, Santa Cruz, San Francisco). Right to Try state law.

name: United States - Texas
general_notes: Right to Try state law. Large medical center presence (Texas Medical Center). Active clinical trial scene. Generally conservative regulatory environment.

name: United States - Florida
general_notes: Right to Try state law. Large elderly population drives regenerative medicine interest. Multiple stem cell clinics operating in regulatory gray zones.

name: Australia
general_notes: TGA rescheduled psilocybin and MDMA for therapeutic use (July 2023) for PTSD and treatment-resistant depression. Authorized prescribers only. Strict regulatory framework via TGA Special Access Scheme and Authorized Prescriber Scheme.

name: Switzerland
general_notes: Compassionate use/exceptional authorization for psychedelic therapy (LSD, psilocybin, MDMA) via BAG permits. Swissmedic oversight. Assisted dying permitted (Dignitas, etc.). Advanced biotech regulatory environment.

name: Canada
general_notes: Special Access Programme (SAP) for psilocybin and MDMA therapy. Section 56 exemptions for psychedelics. MAID (Medical Assistance in Dying) legal federally since 2016, expanded 2021. Generally progressive regulatory stance on emerging therapies.

name: Mexico
general_notes: Growing medical tourism for stem cell therapies (less restrictive regulations). Some clinics operating with minimal oversight. Ibogaine clinics for addiction in Baja region. Regulatory quality variable.

name: Honduras - Próspera ZEDE
general_notes: Special Economic Development Zone (ZEDE) on Roatán Island. Semi-autonomous jurisdiction with its own regulatory framework. Gene therapy, stem cell, and innovative therapeutic hubs developing. Light-touch regulation, attracting biotech investment. Legal status of ZEDEs contested under Honduran law.

name: Netherlands
general_notes: Longstanding truffle (psilocybin sclerotia) legality. Euthanasia legal for unbearable suffering with strict criteria. Advanced medical research environment.

name: Germany
general_notes: Growing psychedelic research hub (MIND Foundation, Charité Berlin). Cannabis legalized 2024. Assisted dying partially legal after 2020 Constitutional Court ruling. Strong regulatory frameworks.

name: United Kingdom
general_notes: Psychedelic clinical trials active (COMPASS Pathways, Imperial College). Strict scheduling of psychedelics. Assisted dying debates ongoing (no legal framework yet outside Scotland proposals).

name: Israel
general_notes: Leading stem cell research country. MDMA/PTSD clinical trials. Growing medical innovation ecosystem. Compassionate use pathways available.

name: Jamaica
general_notes: Psilocybin mushrooms are legal (never scheduled). Growing psilocybin retreat industry. Limited formal regulatory oversight for therapy programs. Variable quality of providers.

name: Thailand
general_notes: Medical tourism hub for stem cells, regenerative medicine, cosmetic procedures. Growing psilocybin retreat industry in Chiang Mai/Bangkok. Light regulatory oversight. Variable quality—from excellent Bangkok hospitals to unregulated clinics.

name: Spain
general_notes: IVF with PGT widely available, less restrictive than many EU countries. Assisted dying legal since 2021 (Organic Law 3/2021). Growing psychedelic research. Good medical tourism infrastructure, especially Barcelona, Madrid.

name: Turkey
general_notes: Major medical tourism destination (Istanbul, Ankara). Stem cell therapies, hair transplants, cosmetic surgery at lower costs. Regulatory oversight variable. Currency advantage for Western patients (Turkish Lira devaluation).

name: India
general_notes: World's largest IVF/fertility tourism market. Stem cell clinics widespread (quality varies). Ayurvedic/traditional medicine integration. Extremely low costs (50-80% less than US). Regulatory oversight weak, high variability in clinic quality.

name: Brazil
general_notes: Large stem cell and regenerative medicine market. Ayahuasca retreat industry (Amazon, São Paulo). Growing cosmetic tourism. Regulatory body ANVISA oversees but enforcement inconsistent.

name: Costa Rica
general_notes: Established medical tourism destination. Stem cell clinics, fertility treatments, cosmetic surgery. CIMA hospitals provide quality infrastructure. Psychedelic retreats growing (psilocybin decriminalized informally). Moderate regulatory oversight.

name: United Arab Emirates (Dubai)
general_notes: Luxury medical tourism hub. Cutting-edge regenerative medicine clinics. Stem cells, exosomes, high-dose micronutrient IVs. Extremely high prices. Regulatory oversight: DHA (Dubai Health Authority) high standards. Minimal psychedelic access.

name: South Korea
general_notes: Advanced biotech hub. Stem cell research leading globally. Placentophagy and placental-derived therapies popular. Anti-aging/longevity medicine trend. High regulatory standards in Seoul/major cities. Medical tourism growing.

name: Greece
general_notes: IVF tourism destination (PGT available, lower costs than Western EU). Mediterranean lifestyle health tourism. Emerging psychedelic research. Healthcare quality high, costs moderate vs. Central/Northern Europe.

name: Belgium
general_notes: Euthanasia/assisted dying legal since 2002 (one of first). No age minimum (minors can access with parental consent). Psychedelic research hub (VUB Brussels). IVF widely available. High regulatory standards.

name: Sweden
general_notes: Progressive healthcare system. Psychedelic research active (Karolinska). Some stem cell therapies available. Assisted dying debates ongoing but no legal framework yet. High healthcare standards, expensive.

name: Japan
general_notes: Advanced medical technology and biohacking culture. Stem cell research strong. Peptide therapies available. Regulatory framework restrictive (fewer regenerative medicine clinics than expected). Medical tourism less developed than Thailand/Korea.

name: Singapore
general_notes: Biomedical hub with highest regulatory standards in Asia. Stem cell/regenerative medicine research. Expensive but high quality. Limited psychedelic access. Strict drug laws.

name: Chile
general_notes: Most developed healthcare system in Latin America. IVF widely available. Growing stem cell tourism. Psilocybin decriminalization movements. Moderate regulatory oversight, good infrastructure in Santiago.

name: Argentina
general_notes: Buenos Aires: growing medical tourism destination. Fertility treatments, cosmetic surgery, stem cells. Currency advantage (peso devaluation). Moderate regulatory oversight. Quality variable by clinic.

name: South Africa
general_notes: Leading African biotech hub (Cape Town, Johannesburg). Stem cell clinics, fertility tourism. Regulatory oversight through SAHPRA (South African Health Products Regulatory Authority). Quality clinics available at lower cost than Western countries.

name: Philippines
general_notes: Emerging medical tourism destination. Stem cell clinics, fertility treatment. Lower costs than Thailand. Regulatory oversight weak (FDA equivalent has limited enforcement). Quality variable.

name: Poland
general_notes: Growing medical tourism hub (Warsaw, Krakow). Fertility treatments, stem cells, regenerative medicine. EU medical standards but lower costs. Psychedelic research active. Good balance of cost/quality.

name: Portugal
general_notes: Decriminalized all drugs (2001 onward—consumption is 'disorderly conduct' not criminal). Growing psychedelic retreat/research centers. IVF tourism destination. Lisbon/Porto wellness tourism hub. Moderate costs, good infrastructure.

name: France
general_notes: Strong healthcare system. Some stem cell therapies via academic research. Assisted dying: recent debates, no legal framework yet. Psychedelic research growing (Paris, universities). High costs, excellent quality.
